item.title: DisciplinaJudicialAI
item.description:
Field Detail
What it solves Conversational assistant that guides judicial servants on the disciplinary regime (Laws 1952 of 2019, 2094 of 2021 and 270 of 1996), without advice on specific cases.
Status Published, with a public demo.
Scope General guidance. It does not replace advice from a lawyer and does not handle specific cases.
License MIT, “Copyright (c) 2025 Daniel”.
Code HammerDev99/disciplinajudicialai
Demo disciplinajudicialai.streamlit.app (in Spanish). The demo uses third-party AI services. Do not enter personal data or information from real cases.
Started First commit: 6 March 2026.
Recognition None.
Measured result No public figures; code and demo open.
Authorship Built by the author from a template by another author (template author’s profile), with the author’s own equipment and accounts, without any commission or instruction from any entity or office.

What it does

  • Explains the stages and deadlines of the disciplinary process.
  • Guides users on how offences are classified, the sanctions and the rights of the person under investigation.

Technologies

Python, Streamlit, the OpenAI Assistants API and the texts of the cited laws.

Design decisions

Streamlit assistant on the OpenAI API with a closed body of legal sources (Constitution, General Disciplinary Code, special regime of the Judicial Branch, internal control and competencies); general normative guidance, never a judgment on a case. No access to case files.

How it was tested

Test questions per user profile (court staff, employees, lawyers, persons under investigation, students) checked against the cited rule; manual review; no published benchmark.

Known limits

It is not legal advice; it does not look up the status of any case; it does not issue judgments of liability; it depends on the corpus loaded being current; the demo uses third-party AI services.

Personal free-software tool, published in a personal capacity. It does not represent the Judicial Branch; using it in a court office requires the corresponding institutional authorizations.

item.title: TYBABot
item.description:
Field Detail
What it solves Conversational assistant that guides users on Justicia XXI Web (TYBA), Colombia’s court case management system, based on the system’s procedures manual (August 2023 version).
Status Published, with a public demo.
License MIT, “Copyright (c) 2025 Daniel”.
Code HammerDev99/TYBABot
Demo tybabot.streamlit.app (in Spanish). The demo uses third-party AI services. Do not enter personal data or information from real cases.
Started First commit: 19 September 2025.
Recognition None.
Measured result No public figures; code and demo open.
Authorship Built by the author from a template by another author (template author’s profile), with the author’s own equipment and accounts, without any commission or instruction from any entity or office.

What it does

  • Answers questions about electronic documents, case entries, filings, notifications and signatures in Justicia XXI Web.
  • Lets users upload documents and export the conversation to PDF.

Technologies

Python, Streamlit and the OpenAI Assistants API.

Design decisions

Conversational assistant in Streamlit on the OpenAI API, using the Justicia XXI Web procedures manual as its document base and answers limited to general guidance; no access to the real system or to case data. Adaptation of an MIT project by another author, credited in the footer.

How it was tested

Test questions per scenario (court staff, clerks, lawyers, administrators, students) compared against the manual; manual review of answers; no published benchmark.

Known limits

The document base goes only as far as the manual in force in August 2023; it is not technical support and does not replace official channels; it can be wrong (hallucinations) and says so; the demo uses third-party AI services, so personal data or real case information must not be entered.

Personal free-software tool, published in a personal capacity. It does not represent the Judicial Branch; using it in a court office requires the corresponding institutional authorizations.

item.title: AgilEx (formerly GestionExpedienteElectronico)
item.description:
Field Detail
What it solves Creates and fills in the electronic index of a court case file from the metadata of the files in a folder, following Agreement PCSJA20-11567 of 2020.
Status Published.
License MIT, “Copyright (c) 2022 Daniel Arbeláez”.
Code HammerDev99/GestionExpedienteElectronico_Version1
Documentation docs.agilex.sprintjudicial.com (in Spanish)
Started First commit: 5 January 2022. Registered with the DNDA (Colombian copyright office) on 3 November 2022 (Book 13, Volume 92, Entry 259), version 1.
Recognition The author was a member of team Marduk, winner of the 1st JusticIALab Innovation Contest 2024, Data-Driven Justice category (Superior Council of the Judiciary news, 13 December 2024, in Spanish).
Measured result 2,466 downloads · 9 releases on GitHub as of 30 October 2026 (releases)
Authorship Version 1 (2022): personal project of the author, developed with the author’s own equipment and accounts, without any commission or instruction from any entity or office.

What it does

  • Extracts metadata (page count, dates, format and size) from PDF, Word and Excel files.
  • Works in three modes: single folder, case file and multiple case files.
  • Validates the unique case identifier (CUI) and the folder structure.
  • Writes the index into an .xlsm template.

Technologies

Python, Tkinter, pandas, PyPDF2, xlwings, PyInstaller and MkDocs.

Design decisions

Desktop application for Windows, with no server or account, because case files sit in local or network folders and must not leave the computer. The index is built only from file metadata (name, date, size, pages), never from their content. Index structure follows Agreement PCSJA20-11567 of 2020. Distributed through releases signed by the author; the updater only notifies, with no automatic download.

How it was tested

Automated tests in src/test (logging configuration, resource management, public-repository hygiene) run on every change; manual tests on sample folders with fictitious names; nine published versions with a changelog.

Known limits

Windows only; relies on the folder following the expected structure; does not validate document content or detect duplicates; page counts depend on PDF integrity.

Personal free-software tool, published in a personal capacity. It does not represent the Judicial Branch; using it in a court office requires the corresponding institutional authorizations.
